# AGENT.md: make this product's chat page You are a coding agent in the repository of a product that lives inside a conversation: a bot, an assistant, a support agent, a chat-first app. The team picked this format. There is no hero, no band and no app window: **the page is the conversation.** It opens on the top of a thread and the first message arrives on its own. Each next message comes as the visitor scrolls (or by itself), the product appears inline as rich cards the person taps, and the last message is the call to action. Opened with `?record&ratio=9:16`, the same page reads as a phone screen recording, ready to post on X. It only works if the conversation is **real**: words the product actually says, tools it actually calls, cards it actually renders. An invented reply is a claim about what the product can do, so don't write one. Read `tour/README.md` once for the engine and `_chat/README.md` for the chat kit. Then work through this in order. ## 0. Where things are ``` index.html the page: one
. The window holds the header, the thread and the composer. chat/section.html the same markup as it came; edit index.html chat/script.js sizes, chapters, the taps inside cards ("after"), the camera chat/section.css the stage: the column, the margins (chapter index, the one control) chat/section.js the beat driver: plays message by message; a scroll brings the next one _chat/ the chat kit: chat.css (the look, its tokens) and chat.js (the thread → the steps) tour/ the engine (tour.js, tour.css), snapshot.py, README.md. Don't edit. kit/ the placeholder kit ``` (In the StyleFeatures repo, `python3 templates/scaffolds/sections/demo/tour/export.py --format chat` makes this layout.) Serve the folder with any static server, e.g. `python3 -m http.server 8000`. ## 1. Learn the product (15 minutes, before writing anything) - **Name and voice.** The product's exact name (and which word deserves the italic), how it introduces itself (its real greeting or system prompt's self-description), its avatar or mark, its status line. - **What it does in a conversation.** List its tools/actions (function definitions, an MCP server, intents, slash commands) and the **card components** it renders in messages: confirmations, pickers, charts, forms, files, galleries, buttons. Find them in the code (`components/messages/*`, `cards/*`, block kits, adaptive cards, Storybook stories). - **The way in.** The real install or sign-up path for the closing card: an "add to workspace" link, an app store page, a web app URL, pricing words, what it works with. Never invent a claim, a number or a customer. ## 2. Harvest a real conversation Pick **3–4 exchanges** that show the core loop, one idea each (they become the chapters). Find them, in this order: 1. **Fixtures and tests**: recorded conversations, `__fixtures__`, eval sets, e2e tests that replay a chat, seed data for a demo workspace, Storybook stories of a message list. These are reviewed and safe to publish. 2. **Onboarding and docs**: the suggested prompts in the empty state, quick replies, examples in the README or docs. 3. **A live run against a demo account**: start the dev server with seed data, have the conversation for real, and copy the transcript from the API response or the logs, including each tool call's name, arguments and result. Use the words verbatim (trim, don't rewrite). Never use a real customer's conversation or data. ## 3. Put it in the thread The thread in `index.html` is the script: each `.ck-row` is one message, in order (`_chat/README.md` has the grammar). For each message: - **the person**: `
` with the text in `.ck-bubble`. It is typed into the composer and sent. If the person taps a quick reply instead, give the row `data-via="@that-chip"`. - **the agent's words**: `
` with the text in `.ck-text[data-stream]` (keep their markdown rendering: lists, bold, code). It streams in word by word after the typing dots. - **a tool call**: `data-kind="tool"` with the real server/tool name, the real arguments in `.ck-args`, the real result (trimmed) in `.ck-out`, and `data-done` set to what the product shows when it finishes. - **a card**: the product's real component, inside the row (`.ck-card[data-ck-in]` is the placeholder frame). Delete the placeholder rows you don't use. Keep the `.ck-start` block (the first frame) and fill it in. ## 4. Use their real cards The cards are what sell the product; they must be the product's own. **Web-rendered cards: harvest them** with `tour/snapshot.py`, one fragment per state, from Storybook or the dev server: ```sh uv run tour/snapshot.py "http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=cards-booking--default" --selector "#storybook-root > *" \ --size 460x400 --out chat/fragments/booking.html --scope booking \ --hook "button:nth-of-type(2)=slot-2" --hook "button.primary=book" uv run tour/snapshot.py "http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=cards-booking--booked" --selector "#storybook-root > *" \ --size 460x400 --out chat/fragments/booked.html --scope booked ``` - `--size` is the card's width in the thread (about 460 design px; 340 on phones), height generous. - `--hook "css=name"` marks what the script taps, so `script.js` can say `click('@slot-2')`. - Put two states in a `[data-ck-swap]` (first the picker, then the result) and load each with `
`; `section.js` fetches them before measuring. In `script.js`, `after: { rowName: [click('@slot-2'), set('@slot-2', { class: '+is-on' }), click('@book'), tween('@booking-swap', '--swap', 0, 1)] }` taps through them. - Don't hand-edit fragments; re-capture. Small changes (a picked state) are `set()` on a hook. **Native or server-rendered cards** (Slack blocks, Teams adaptive cards, SwiftUI): rebuild them in HTML/CSS with their exact tokens and copy, next to a screenshot of the real one until they match. Images inside cards are the product's own sample content or kit placeholders (`.ph`), never a real person's photos. ## 5. Make it look like theirs Set the chat kit's tokens on `.ck-app` in `chat/section.css` (`--ck-bg`, `--ck-card`, `--ck-me` for the person's bubble, `--ck-line`, `--ck-accent`, `--ck-radius`) and the fonts to theirs. Put their mark in `[data-ck-avatar]` and `.ck-av-l`. Keep the calm: one accent, hairlines, no gradients. Don't copy any other product's chat look. ## 6. The script and the pacing (`chat/script.js`) - **35–50 seconds.** 3–4 chapters, one exchange each; `chapters` names the row each starts at (`'02 / 04'`, a title with one `` word). They become the clickable index in the margin and the story in a 16:9 recording. - Pacing lives on the rows: `data-think` (typing dots, .6–1.2 s), `data-read` (held after it), `data-run` (a tool call), `data-cps` (typing speed). Every tap must change something visible; one push-in per chapter at most (`zoom('@card', 'fit', { fill: [.8, .9] })`, then `unzoom()`). - **The ending is the last message**: the `.ck-cta` card with the product's name, one honest line, the real primary link (`href`) and a second one, and the domain. It holds for `outro` seconds. ## 7. Check it - `index.html?t=12.5` freezes any moment. Check right after each tap, mid-stream, and the last frame. - `?record&ratio=9:16&t=…` (a phone: status bar, a fingertip), `?record&ratio=1:1&t=…`, `?record&ratio=16:9&t=…`. Text must be readable in 1:1; nothing cut except by the column's edges. - Play it from the top: the first message arrives by itself; scroll brings the next; scroll up reads back; the control pauses (then each scroll plays one message). On a phone, tap and swipe. With reduced motion, the whole transcript shows still, from the top. - Delete every `.sf-note`, set the page `` and meta description. ## 8. Record and post Open `index.html?record&ratio=9:16` in a tall browser window and record it with **Monet Shot** (crop to the stage, park the real pointer off it; the page draws its own finger). It holds the first frame 1.2 s, plays once and holds on the closing card. Post the export to X with one line and the link. Use `ratio=16:9` for a desktop-first audience (the chapter index shows beside the column) and `1:1` for the feed. ## The painting it sits on Opened on its own, the page sits on *Strolling along the Seashore* by Joaquín Sorolla (public domain), the way Monet Shot frames a take: the site is a sheet with rounded corners and the painting fills the margin. It lives in `backdrop/` (`painting.webp` and a small `backdrop.js`). It turns itself off with `?record` (Monet Shot adds its own painting), with `?bare`, and inside a frame. Keep it, swap `painting.webp` for another, or delete the `backdrop.js` script line in `index.html` to drop it. ## When it's done: record your launch video with Monet Shot [Monet Shot](https://monetshot.pages.dev/) is a free screen recorder, made for pages like this one: it frames every take on a painting and zooms where things happen. Download it for [Mac](https://github.com/SocialAcolyte/monet-shot/releases/download/v0.1.1/MonetShot-0.1.1.zip), [Windows](https://github.com/SocialAcolyte/monet-shot/releases/download/desktop-v0.1.1/MonetShot-0.1.1-windows-x64-setup.exe) or [Linux](https://github.com/SocialAcolyte/monet-shot/releases/download/desktop-v0.1.1/MonetShot-0.1.1-x86_64.AppImage) (Windows and Linux are test builds; other packages are on the [releases page](https://github.com/SocialAcolyte/monet-shot/releases)). 1. Open the finished site with `index.html?record&ratio=16:9&captions=on` (use `ratio=1:1` or `ratio=9:16` for square and vertical posts). Only the stage shows, it plays once from the start, and captions are on, because X autoplays muted. 2. In Monet Shot, pick the browser window, crop to the stage, and park your real pointer off it (the tour draws its own cursor). Record one play-through. 3. Export, and post it with a link to the site. **For the agent:** when the site is finished, end your last message to the person with this step: the full `index.html?record&ratio=16:9&captions=on` link on their real URL (and the 1:1 and 9:16 versions), and the Monet Shot download link above for their computer.

# tour.js: the demo-film engine One engine for every StyleFeatures demo film. A template supplies a window with a product inside it and a script; the engine plays it with a fake cursor, a camera, chapter cards and captions, and drives it from a scroll, a clock, a screen recorder or a frozen `?t=`. Files: | file | what it is | edit it? | |---|---|---| | `tour.js` | the engine: step builders, `Tour`, `include()` | no, it's shared by every format | | `tour.css` | the engine's look: chromes, cursor, card, caption, keys, controls, record stage | no; restyle through its tokens | | `script.js` | this film's script | yes | | `section.html` / `section.css` | this film's band, closing frame and product | yes | | `snapshot.py` | harvests a live screen into a static fragment | no | | `export.py` | copies the whole format out as a standalone folder | no | | `AGENT.md` | the brief for the coding agent that fills it in | read it | Everything on screen is a pure function of one number, `t`, in seconds. Each frame the engine works out the product's state at `t` (classes, attributes, text, CSS variables, scroll positions), the camera, the cursor and the overlays, then writes only what changed. Nothing depends on what happened in earlier frames, so any moment renders on its own, the same way every time. ## Markup ```html
… your product, built at 1200 × 750 design pixels …
…
…
``` The engine adds the chrome, the cursor, ripples, the chapter card, the caption line, key caps, and the driver's controls. The opening band (`data-tour-band`) slides away in the first `intro` seconds; the closing frame (`data-tour-end`) gets `--in` 0→1 at the end and its own CSS decides what that looks like. The root also carries `--tour-band` (1 → 0 over the intro), `--tour-out` (0 → 1 over the outro) and `--tour-p` (0 → 1 over the whole film) for a format's own CSS. `data-tour-band="css"` stops the engine sliding the band away; the format fades or moves it from `--tour-band` instead. **A frame the format draws: `data-tour-frame`.** Put an element with `data-tour-frame` in the stage and lay it out in CSS (a phone's glass, a mat around a screenshot, a different box per ratio). The engine fits the window to it exactly, clips the camera to it (with its `border-radius`), and every zoom stays inside it: the window always covers the frame, so a push-in never shows what's around it. The outro then leaves the window where it is (use `--tour-out` to do something else). Give the frame the window's aspect ratio. `demo/phone` (the glass, beside the text or under it) and `demo/launch-note` (a mat on the page, a different box per recording ratio) use it. ### Window chromes: `data-chrome` | value | looks like | typical `data-size` | |---|---|---| | `browser` | traffic lights, back/forward, an address pill (`data-url`), share/new icons | `1200x750` | | `app` | a macOS title bar with traffic lights and a centred `data-title` | `1200x760` | | `phone` | a dark bezel, a status bar with the time and a notch | `390x844` | | `none` | just rounded corners | anything | | `terminal` | a warm charcoal window, traffic lights, a centred `data-title`; tokens `--tour-term-bg/-bar/-ink/-dim` | `780x548` | **Windows inside the window.** Any element inside the window with a `data-chrome` gets that chrome too, and a frame (`display:flex`, rounded, clipped). With `data-chrome="none"` on the outer window (made transparent in your CSS) it becomes a desk holding, say, a terminal and a browser; the camera pans between them with `zoom()` (`demo/terminal` does this). **A second design size for tall stages.** `data-size-tall="440x820"` on the window (or `sizeTall: [440, 820]` in the script) is used whenever the stage is taller than wide (W/H < .8: phones, 9:16 recordings). The root gets `.is-tall` before anything is measured, so your CSS can re-lay the product for it (stack two panes, say) and the script's targets follow. `demo/split` stacks its panes this way. **A third for squarish stages.** `data-size-square="760x760"` (or `sizeSquare: [760, 760]`) is used when .8 ≤ W/H < 1.15 (1:1 recordings, square-ish windows), and the root gets `.is-square` the same way. Without it those stages use the wide size, as before. `demo/agentic` has all three: a tiled desk (wide), and one live window beside (square) or above (tall) its run sheet. **A height that follows the frame: `auto`.** `data-size="580xauto"` (or `size: [580, 'auto']`, and the same for `sizeTall`) fixes the window's width and takes its height from the `data-tour-frame` at every layout, so the window always has the frame's shape: a full-height column on a wide page, the whole screen on a phone, any recording ratio. For products that read top to bottom (a chat, a feed, a transcript). `demo/chat` and `demo/mcp` use it. Build the product at the design size in plain CSS pixels. The engine scales the whole window, so text stays real text and stays sharp at any zoom. ### Hooks `'@name'` anywhere in a selector means `[data-tour="name"]`. Put `data-tour="…"` on the things the script points at. Pointer targets also choose the cursor: links, buttons, `role=button|tab|switch` get the hand, inputs and `data-tour-cursor="text"` get the I-beam, the rest the arrow (`data-tour-cursor="arrow|pointer|text"` overrides it). While the cursor rests on a target, that target has `.is-hover`; while it's pressed, `.is-press`. Style both so clicks read. ## The script ```js import { click, type, show, hide, set, tween, zoom, unzoom, chapter, caption, pause } from './tour.js'; export default { size: [1200, 750], // window design size (or data-size on the window) enter: [.84, .97], // where the cursor comes in from, as fractions of the window intro: 1.3, // seconds for the opening band to clear (0: no band) outro: 4.5, // seconds held on the closing frame settle: .6, // pause between the last step and the outro still: 17.4, // the moment reduced motion shows fit: [.92, .88, .5], // optional: see below steps: [ … ], }; ``` `fit: [w, h, y]` is for a stage that holds nothing but the window (a panel beside text, with no card or band over it): the window may take `w` of the stage's width and `h` of its height, centred at `y` (default .5), and push-ins aim at the middle of the frame. Without it the page layout leaves room for the card and band (`[.74, .7, .47]`). It never changes `?record`. `demo/chapters` uses it. Steps run in order on one clock. **Pointer steps** take time and the next step waits for them. **Side steps** start at the current moment and the next step starts with them, so `click('@create'), hide('@modal'), show('@toast')` hides the modal and shows the toast as the click lands. Every step takes: `at: 12.5` pin it to an absolute time · `wait: .4` start this much later · `parallel: true` (pointer steps) don't hold up the next step · `block: true` (side steps) do hold it up. ### Pointer steps | step | what happens | options (defaults) | |---|---|---| | `move(sel)` | glides there on a gentle arc, smootherstep | `dur` .9, `aim` [x, y] fractions of the target, `cursor` | | `click(sel)` | moves, presses (cursor shrinks, target gets `.is-press`), ripple | as `move` | | `dblclick(sel)` | moves, two presses, two ripples | as `move` | | `hover(sel)` | moves and rests (`.is-hover` on the target) | `dur` .9, `hold` .6 | | `type(sel, text)` | characters appear in `sel` at a human, uneven pace; `.is-caret` while typing, then blinking | `cps` 13, `rhythm` (below), `lead` (s of steady caret before the first key), `caret` (s it blinks after the last key, 1.6), `blink` (absolute time it goes) | | `stream(sel)` | each match appears in turn, like output arriving: gets `.is-in`, and `--in` 0→1 over `dur`. A match's `data-tour-wait="1.2"` adds that pause before it (a slow step) | `every` .06 s, `jitter` .5 (±50 % of `every`; 0 for an exact beat), `dur` .08 | | `drag(handle, o)` | moves to the handle, presses, then drives a value while the cursor stays on the handle | `approach` .8, `dur` 1.2, `prop` + `from` + `to` (+ `el` to put the property on another element), `text: [sel, v => label]`, or `onto: sel` to carry the handle itself there | | `scroll(sel, to)` | scrolls an element; `to` is px, `'50%'`, `'end'` or a selector inside it | `dur` 1.4, `offset` 16 | | `key(keys)` | key caps on screen, e.g. `key(['⌘', 'K'])` | `dur` .9, `hold` 1.4 | | `pause(s)` | a beat | | | `tap(sel)` | the same step as `click`; reads better in a touch film | as `click` | | `longpress(sel)` | moves, presses and holds; it fires (`.is-press` stays on, a ripple) after `hold`, and the finger stays down `lift` longer while the next steps start (open a context menu there) | `dur` .9, `hold` .7, `lift` .35 | | `swipe(sel, o)` | a finger flick that starts on `sel`: lands, travels `by` [dx, dy] window px speeding up, lifts while still moving. What it moves follows it 1:1, then coasts to rest over `coast` s with the speed it was let go at. `scroll: to` scrolls `sel` (or `in: sel`) to `to` (px, `'50%'`, `'end'`, a selector; `offset`); `prop` + `from` + `to` (+ `el`) drives a CSS variable instead (a carousel, a sheet dragged down), `follow` (.45) of it under the finger | `approach` .7, `by` [0, -220], `dur` .36, `coast` .8 (0: a slow drag that ends at rest), `settle` (when the next step starts, `coast` × .5) | `type`'s `rhythm`: unset is the even, slightly uneven pace it always had. `'human'` types like a person at a keyboard: a beat between words, a reach for symbols (`- / . : =`), a pause after punctuation, doubled letters run together, the odd hesitation. `'stream'` lands the text in chunks of 1–5 characters, the way a model's reply arrives. `stream()` is for whole lines or blocks; hide them in CSS until `.is-in` (`.line{display:none}.line.is-in{display:block}`) so they take space only once they've arrived. The cursor's path between targets is a smootherstep glide with a slight bow (direction-dependent, never a straight line) and a slightly early peak speed, like a hand. It never teleports: each move starts where the last one ended. **A finger instead of a cursor.** `pointer: 'touch'` in the script (or `data-pointer="touch"` on the root, `?pointer=touch`) swaps the arrow for a fingertip: a soft translucent dot, 44 window px, that is part of the screen, so it zooms with it. It is unseen between touches (a hand travelling isn't on the glass); a shadow gathers for a fifth of a second before contact, the dot flattens and darkens while pressed (`.is-down` on `.tour-cur`), and lifts away. `drag` and `swipe` carry it across the glass. Give each touch a beat: the `dur` before it is the hand travelling. Restyle the dot with `--tour-touch` / `--tour-touch-down`. `demo/phone` is the worked example. **More than one pointer.** Any pointer step with `by: 'agent'` moves a second cursor on its own track (any name works; steps without `by` move the usual one, `'main'`). Describe each in the script: ```js pointers: { main: { label: 'You', idle: 1.4 }, // a tag on the person's cursor; it fades after 1.4 s still agent: { label: 'Agent', look: 'agent', bow: .2, enter: [.33, .2] }, }, steps: [ click('@search', { by: 'agent', tag: 'search_code' }), …, click('@approve', { from: [.99, 1.03] }) ] ``` A second pointer is an arrow in `--tour-agent` (look `'agent'`) with a label tag beside it; `tag` on a step adds a word to that label from then on (the tool it's using, "waiting for you"). `bow` scales the curve of its path (0 is a straight, machine-like line), `enter` is where it first appears, `shapes: true` lets it take the hand and I-beam too. `idle: s` fades a pointer out once it has been still that long and back in when it next moves; `from: [x, y]` (fractions of the window) on a step starts that move there instead, so a hand can come back in from off the edge. Each pointer's clicks ripple in its own colour (`.tour-ring[data-who]`), and `.tour-cur[data-who="…"]` lets a page hide one (`demo/agentic` hides the person's cursor on the live page, where the visitor is the person). Touch mode (`pointer: 'touch'`) applies to the main pointer only. ### Side steps | step | what happens | options | |---|---|---| | `show(sel)` / `hide(sel)` | tweens `--in` to 1 / 0 on every match; your CSS uses `opacity: var(--in)` etc. | `dur` .35 / .28, `stagger` | | `set(sel, changes)` | instant: `{class: '+on -off'}`, `{text: 'Copied'}`, `{'--x': 2}`, `{'data-view': 'room'}`, `{attr: null}` removes | | | `tween(sel, prop, from, to)` | animates a CSS variable, `'text'` (with `fmt`) or `'scrollTop'` | `dur` .45, `fmt`, `stagger` | | `zoom(sel, z)` | camera pushes in on the target. `z` a number, or `'fit'` to frame the element at `fill` of the frame | `dur` 1.3, `fill` .66 (or `[wide, stacked]`, e.g. `[.76, .96]`: tighter on 1:1 and phones, where the window is small), `aim`, `max` 2.6 (the most a `'fit'` may push in: raise it for a big window such as a whole board), `arc` 0 (0–1: pull back by that share mid-flight and push in again, so a long pan reads as a camera crossing; `demo/canvas`) | | `unzoom()` | camera back to the whole window | `dur` 1.3 | | `chapter(n, title, line)` | the card: `'02 / 05'`, a title with one `` word, one line; until the next chapter | `until` | | `caption(text)` | the caption line, until the next caption | `dur` 4 | | `mark(name)` | nothing on screen: a named moment. `tour.api.marks` lists them in order (`{ t, name }`) and `marks[name]` is that moment's time, so a page can seek to one or stop at the next (`demo/chat`'s beats, `demo/mcp`'s tabs) | | `show`, `hide` and `tween` take `ease`: `'out'` (decelerate), `'ios'` (a critically damped spring, UIKit's pushes and sheets), `'spring'` (overshoots by about 3 %), `'linear'`, or any `(t) => t` function. The default is smootherstep. The curves are exported as `eases`. `data-tour-follow` on a scrolling element (a terminal, a chat thread, a log) keeps its newest content in view every frame, so lines that `stream()` in push the old ones up. `data-tour-grow` on an element that should take height as it arrives (a message in a thread, a folded panel): the engine measures its natural height into `--h` (design px, innermost first, before targets are measured, and again on every relayout), so your CSS can open it with `--in` and let go once it's in: `max-height: max(calc(var(--in) * var(--h)), calc((var(--in) - .999) * 1e7px))`. Rows arrive smoothly and may change size afterwards. `../_chat/chat.css` is the worked example. Elements that `show()` controls should start hidden in CSS (`--in: 0`). Anything the script changes is reset when you seek backwards, because every value is recomputed from `t`. ### The camera `zoom` pushes in on a point and keeps the window filling the frame: it borrows Monet Shot's fit clamp, so a push-in never pans past the window's edge (the window is either wholly inside the frame or covers it). Zoom levels move on a log scale, so in and out feel even. Numbers are multiplied by 1.15 on portrait stages, where the window is small (not inside a `data-tour-frame`, which the window always fills). `?camera=off` turns all push-ins off. On stacked stages (1:1, 9:16, phones) the cursor fades out rather than being drawn outside the window's frame. ### Measuring Targets are measured in the window's own pixels, against the product as it is at the moment each step happens (so a button inside a modal that opens two steps earlier is measured with the modal open), and measured again whenever the layout can change: fonts loading, the stage resizing, your CSS. Edit the product freely; the script follows. ## The card and caption keep out of the way The chapter card and the caption never sit on what the tour is doing. Each frame the engine checks the cursor (or fingertip) and any text being typed (`type`) or streamed in (`stream`), with its last second after. If the card would cover it, the card slides to the other side of the stage; if both sides are busy it steps out, and it comes home once the spot has been clear for .8 s. The caption lifts to the top. Outside `?record` the card carries a × that hides the cards for the rest of the visit; recordings have none. Nothing to configure. Style both so clicks read. ## The script ```js import { click, type, show, hide, set, tween, zoom, unzoom, chapter, caption, pause } from './tour.js'; export default { size: [1200, 750], // window design size (or data-size on the window) enter: [.84, .97], // where the cursor comes in from, as fractions of the window intro: 1.3, // seconds for the opening band to clear (0: no band) outro: 4.5, // seconds held on the closing frame settle: .6, // pause between the last step and the outro still: 17.4, // the moment reduced motion shows fit: [.92, .88, .5], // optional: see below steps: [ … ], }; ``` `fit: [w, h, y]` is for a stage that holds nothing but the window (a panel beside text, with no card or band over it): the window may take `w` of the stage's width and `h` of its height, centred at `y` (default .5), and push-ins aim at the middle of the frame. Without it the page layout leaves room for the card and band (`[.74, .7, .47]`). It never changes `?record`. `demo/chapters` uses it. Steps run in order on one clock. **Pointer steps** take time and the next step waits for them. **Side steps** start at the current moment and the next step starts with them, so `click('@create'), hide('@modal'), show('@toast')` hides the modal and shows the toast as the click lands. Every step takes: `at: 12.5` pin it to an absolute time · `wait: .4` start this much later · `parallel: true` (pointer steps) don't hold up the next step · `block: true` (side steps) do hold it up. ### Pointer steps | step | what happens | options (defaults) | |---|---|---| | `move(sel)` | glides there on a gentle arc, smootherstep | `dur` .9, `aim` [x, y] fractions of the target, `cursor` | | `click(sel)` | moves, presses (cursor shrinks, target gets `.is-press`), ripple | as `move` | | `dblclick(sel)` | moves, two presses, two ripples | as `move` | | `hover(sel)` | moves and rests (`.is-hover` on the target) | `dur` .9, `hold` .6 | | `type(sel, text)` | characters appear in `sel` at a human, uneven pace; `.is-caret` while typing, then blinking | `cps` 13, `rhythm` (below), `lead` (s of steady caret before the first key), `caret` (s it blinks after the last key, 1.6), `blink` (absolute time it goes) | | `stream(sel)` | each match appears in turn, like output arriving: gets `.is-in`, and `--in` 0→1 over `dur`. A match's `data-tour-wait="1.2"` adds that pause before it (a slow step) | `every` .06 s, `jitter` .5 (±50 % of `every`; 0 for an exact beat), `dur` .08 | | `drag(handle, o)` | moves to the handle, presses, then drives a value while the cursor stays on the handle | `approach` .8, `dur` 1.2, `prop` + `from` + `to` (+ `el` to put the property on another element), `text: [sel, v => label]`, or `onto: sel` to carry the handle itself there | | `scroll(sel, to)` | scrolls an element; `to` is px, `'50%'`, `'end'` or a selector inside it | `dur` 1.4, `offset` 16 | | `key(keys)` | key caps on screen, e.g. `key(['⌘', 'K'])` | `dur` .9, `hold` 1.4 | | `pause(s)` | a beat | | | `tap(sel)` | the same step as `click`; reads better in a touch film | as `click` | | `longpress(sel)` | moves, presses and holds; it fires (`.is-press` stays on, a ripple) after `hold`, and the finger stays down `lift` longer while the next steps start (open a context menu there) | `dur` .9, `hold` .7, `lift` .35 | | `swipe(sel, o)` | a finger flick that starts on `sel`: lands, travels `by` [dx, dy] window px speeding up, lifts while still moving. What it moves follows it 1:1, then coasts to rest over `coast` s with the speed it was let go at. `scroll: to` scrolls `sel` (or `in: sel`) to `to` (px, `'50%'`, `'end'`, a selector; `offset`); `prop` + `from` + `to` (+ `el`) drives a CSS variable instead (a carousel, a sheet dragged down), `follow` (.45) of it under the finger | `approach` .7, `by` [0, -220], `dur` .36, `coast` .8 (0: a slow drag that ends at rest), `settle` (when the next step starts, `coast` × .5) | `type`'s `rhythm`: unset is the even, slightly uneven pace it always had. `'human'` types like a person at a keyboard: a beat between words, a reach for symbols (`- / . : =`), a pause after punctuation, doubled letters run together, the odd hesitation. `'stream'` lands the text in chunks of 1–5 characters, the way a model's reply arrives. `stream()` is for whole lines or blocks; hide them in CSS until `.is-in` (`.line{display:none}.line.is-in{display:block}`) so they take space only once they've arrived. The cursor's path between targets is a smootherstep glide with a slight bow (direction-dependent, never a straight line) and a slightly early peak speed, like a hand. It never teleports: each move starts where the last one ended. **A finger instead of a cursor.** `pointer: 'touch'` in the script (or `data-pointer="touch"` on the root, `?pointer=touch`) swaps the arrow for a fingertip: a soft translucent dot, 44 window px, that is part of the screen, so it zooms with it. It is unseen between touches (a hand travelling isn't on the glass); a shadow gathers for a fifth of a second before contact, the dot flattens and darkens while pressed (`.is-down` on `.tour-cur`), and lifts away. `drag` and `swipe` carry it across the glass. Give each touch a beat: the `dur` before it is the hand travelling. Restyle the dot with `--tour-touch` / `--tour-touch-down`. `demo/phone` is the worked example. **More than one pointer.** Any pointer step with `by: 'agent'` moves a second cursor on its own track (any name works; steps without `by` move the usual one, `'main'`). Describe each in the script: ```js pointers: { main: { label: 'You', idle: 1.4 }, // a tag on the person's cursor; it fades after 1.4 s still agent: { label: 'Agent', look: 'agent', bow: .2, enter: [.33, .2] }, }, steps: [ click('@search', { by: 'agent', tag: 'search_code' }), …, click('@approve', { from: [.99, 1.03] }) ] ``` A second pointer is an arrow in `--tour-agent` (look `'agent'`) with a label tag beside it; `tag` on a step adds a word to that label from then on (the tool it's using, "waiting for you"). `bow` scales the curve of its path (0 is a straight, machine-like line), `enter` is where it first appears, `shapes: true` lets it take the hand and I-beam too. `idle: s` fades a pointer out once it has been still that long and back in when it next moves; `from: [x, y]` (fractions of the window) on a step starts that move there instead, so a hand can come back in from off the edge. Each pointer's clicks ripple in its own colour (`.tour-ring[data-who]`), and `.tour-cur[data-who="…"]` lets a page hide one (`demo/agentic` hides the person's cursor on the live page, where the visitor is the person). Touch mode (`pointer: 'touch'`) applies to the main pointer only. ### Side steps | step | what happens | options | |---|---|---| | `show(sel)` / `hide(sel)` | tweens `--in` to 1 / 0 on every match; your CSS uses `opacity: var(--in)` etc. | `dur` .35 / .28, `stagger` | | `set(sel, changes)` | instant: `{class: '+on -off'}`, `{text: 'Copied'}`, `{'--x': 2}`, `{'data-view': 'room'}`, `{attr: null}` removes | | | `tween(sel, prop, from, to)` | animates a CSS variable, `'text'` (with `fmt`) or `'scrollTop'` | `dur` .45, `fmt`, `stagger` | | `zoom(sel, z)` | camera pushes in on the target. `z` a number, or `'fit'` to frame the element at `fill` of the frame | `dur` 1.3, `fill` .66 (or `[wide, stacked]`, e.g. `[.76, .96]`: tighter on 1:1 and phones, where the window is small), `aim`, `max` 2.6 (the most a `'fit'` may push in: raise it for a big window such as a whole board), `arc` 0 (0–1: pull back by that share mid-flight and push in again, so a long pan reads as a camera crossing; `demo/canvas`) | | `unzoom()` | camera back to the whole window | `dur` 1.3 | | `chapter(n, title, line)` | the card: `'02 / 05'`, a title with one `` word, one line; until the next chapter | `until` | | `caption(text)` | the caption line, until the next caption | `dur` 4 | | `mark(name)` | nothing on screen: a named moment. `tour.api.marks` lists them in order (`{ t, name }`) and `marks[name]` is that moment's time, so a page can seek to one or stop at the next (`demo/chat`'s beats, `demo/mcp`'s tabs) | | `show`, `hide` and `tween` take `ease`: `'out'` (decelerate), `'ios'` (a critically damped spring, UIKit's pushes and sheets), `'spring'` (overshoots by about 3 %), `'linear'`, or any `(t) => t` function. The default is smootherstep. The curves are exported as `eases`. `data-tour-follow` on a scrolling element (a terminal, a chat thread, a log) keeps its newest content in view every frame, so lines that `stream()` in push the old ones up. `data-tour-grow` on an element that should take height as it arrives (a message in a thread, a folded panel): the engine measures its natural height into `--h` (design px, innermost first, before targets are measured, and again on every relayout), so your CSS can open it with `--in` and let go once it's in: `max-height: max(calc(var(--in) * var(--h)), calc((var(--in) - .999) * 1e7px))`. Rows arrive smoothly and may change size afterwards. `../_chat/chat.css` is the worked example. Elements that `show()` controls should start hidden in CSS (`--in: 0`). Anything the script changes is reset when you seek backwards, because every value is recomputed from `t`. ### The camera `zoom` pushes in on a point and keeps the window filling the frame: it borrows Monet Shot's fit clamp, so a push-in never pans past the window's edge (the window is either wholly inside the frame or covers it). Zoom levels move on a log scale, so in and out feel even. Numbers are multiplied by 1.15 on portrait stages, where the window is small (not inside a `data-tour-frame`, which the window always fills). `?camera=off` turns all push-ins off. On stacked stages (1:1, 9:16, phones) the cursor fades out rather than being drawn outside the window's frame. ### Measuring Targets are measured in the window's own pixels, against the product as it is at the moment each step happens (so a button inside a modal that opens two steps earlier is measured with the modal open), and measured again whenever the layout can change: fonts loading, the stage resizing, your CSS. Edit the product freely; the script follows. ## The card and caption keep out of the way The chapter card and the caption never sit on what the tour is doing. Each frame the engine checks the cursor (or fingertip) and any text being typed (`type`) or streamed in (`stream`), with its last second after. If the card would cover it, the card slides to the other side of the stage; if both sides are busy it steps out, and it comes home once the spot has been clear for .8 s. The caption lifts to the top. Outside `?record` the card carries a × that hides the cards for the rest of the visit; recordings have none. Nothing to configure. In stacked layouts (phones, 9:16) the card already sits under the window, so nothing moves. ## Drivers | driver | how | when | |---|---|---| | `scroll` (default) | `data-driver="scroll"`. Never in `?record`, which plays once. `begin()` (or `tour.api.begin()`) starts it from code, e.g. when it scrolls into view. | a short feature loop: `demo/launch-note` | | reduced motion | shows `still` with the camera off and the card on: the whole window, a sensible frame | always on | | `?record` | see below | recording | `data-music="audio/track.mp3"` on the root starts a loop with a fade at the gate. `data-captions`: `record` (default: only in `?record`), `always`, `off`. `data-cursor="off"` hides the cursor; `data-cursor-look="light"` gives a white arrow. ## Recording: `?record` ``` index.html?record&ratio=16:9 16:9, 1:1 or 9:16, centred in the browser window &hold=1.2 seconds held on the first frame before it plays (default 1.2) &camera=off no push-ins (see below) &captions=off no caption line &t=12.5 a frozen frame of the recording, for checking ``` It renders only the stage, at the largest box of that ratio that fits the window, on near-black, with no page, notes, spec card, gate or controls, and sizes the overlays to the stage. The film may sit anywhere in the page, inside another section: everything that isn't the film or one of its ancestors is hidden. It holds the first frame (the title band), plays once from 0 and stops on the closing frame. Captions are on, because X autoplays muted. Record it with **Monet Shot**: pick the browser window, crop to the stage, and export. Two things to know: - Monet Shot zooms on **real** clicks. The tour's clicks are drawn, not real, so Monet Shot sees none and adds no zooms of its own. The tour's camera therefore stays **on** by default. If you would rather place zooms yourself on Monet Shot's timeline, use `&camera=off` and you won't get double zooms. - Monet Shot draws its own cursor from the real pointer. Park the real pointer off the recorded window (or set Monet Shot's cursor to hidden) so only the tour's cursor shows. From script: `window.tour` has `seek(t)`, `play()`, `pause()`, `load(script)`, `t`, `duration`, `chapters` and `ready` (a promise that resolves once fonts are in and everything is measured). The root gets a `tour:end` event whenever `play()` reaches the end (any driver). **Several tours in one recorded frame.** A format whose recording is more than one film (two windows racing in `demo/versus`, a whole slide deck in `demo/deck`) makes its own element the record stage and drives the tours itself: ```js import { Tour, recordStage } from './tour.js'; const box = q.has('record') ? recordStage(root) : null; // root becomes the ratio's box, centred on near-black, the rest hidden const a = new Tour(filmA, scriptA, { driver: 'manual', record: 'page' }); // no record stage or auto-play of its own a.render(t); // the page decides t, every frame ``` `recordStage(el)` does for `el` what `?record` does for a single film (the `tour-record` and `sf-clean` classes, `--rw`/`--rh` from `&ratio=`, kept current on resize) and returns `{ w, h, ratio }`. `{ record: 'page' }` on a Tour means: in `?record` stay on the manual driver and let the page play it (captions follow `captions` as usual). Without `?record` it changes nothing. The page then holds the first frame, plays once and honours `&t=` itself. `load(script)` swaps in another script on the same window: every value the old script touched goes back to how the page drew it, then the new script is compiled and measured. `demo/playground` uses it to turn a visitor's clicks into a live script that the engine plays on from, so their clicks get the film's eases. ## Harvested screens: `include()` and `snapshot.py` ```html
